text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Foreign Minister Toomas Ilves said during his visit to the U.S. that countries have agreed to hold a second wave of enlargement. The U.S. government is offering the Baltic states a security pact aimed at integrating them into European and international organisations.
- The government of the southern city of Tartu may have to resign as the council factions are uncertain about which partners to choose.
- The ruling Coalition Party council met on Saturday, March 29, to discuss its internal affairs. Mayor of Tallinn Robert Lepikson declared that he had not left the party.
- Interior ministry chancellor Jaan Toots used ministry cars for personal affairs, a news magazine claims.
- Estonia is a member of the Spitzbergen agreement and has a right to mine coal and other minerals in the region, director of the Ecology Institute reminded.
- The inter-departmental traffic commission proposed to allow a maximum 100-kilometre speed on roads this summer, instead of the present 90-kilometre top speed.
- The international Carnegie Foundation has invited ex-premier Mart Laar to join the advisory chamber of economic reforms as founding member.
- The police are to decide, whether to dismiss the prefect of eastern city Narva for distortion of crime statistics and inadequate control over the activities of the subordinated.
- The human rights situation in Estonia in the past or present has been inadequately studied, rector of the Tartu University Peeter Tulviste said at a history conference.

- Life in Tallinn has become more expensive due to an impending rises of water, heating and electricity rates. Rises of telephone rates, fuel excise and a national motor vehicle tax will come this summer.
- The interest of local investors is the reason for the continued rise of share prices in the Estonian exchange, analysts claim.
- The Finnish border guard is not yet ready for the Estonian passports with bar codes but scanners are to be set up in most checkpoints by May 1.
